q: 1. The degree of saturation in soils can be defined as the ratio of
options: water by weight to the dry soil weight
vol. of water to the gross vol. of soil
vol. of water to vol. of voids in soils
wt. of the water to wt. of soil
explain: Degree of saturation Sr = Volume of water / Volume of voids, expressed as a percentage; it tells how much of the void space is filled with water.

q: 2. The most accurate method of determining the water content in a sample of soil is
explain: Oven drying at 105-110°C to constant weight removes only free/pore water precisely, making it the standard, most accurate laboratory method (IS: 2720 Part 2).

q: 3. Generally soils is considered as
explain: Soil is a three-phase system consisting of solid particles, water, and air voids.

q: 4. Fully saturated soil is considered as
explain: In a fully saturated soil, all voids are filled with water, leaving only two phases: solids and water.

q: 5. Degree of saturation of a soil is generally
explain: The degree of saturation (S) represents the ratio of water volume to void volume, ranging from 0% (dry) to 100% (saturated).

q: 6. The most commonly used specific gravity of a soil in soil mechanics is .............
explain: Grain (true) specific gravity of the solid particles is the value most commonly used and reported in soil mechanics.

q: 7. You are given a sample of soil containing coarse grains to determine its water content, you will use
explain: For coarse-grained soils, the pycnometer method (using known specific gravity) is the standard quick technique to back-calculate water content.

q: 8. The void ratio for saturated soil is equal to the ......... of water content and specific gravity of solid
explain: For saturated soil, e = wG, i.e. void ratio equals the product of water content and specific gravity.

q: 9. The ratio of the volume of air voids to the volume of voids, is called .............
explain: Air content is defined as the ratio of the volume of air voids to the total volume of voids.

q: 10. The ratio of volume of air void to the volume of voids, is known
explain: Air content (ac) is the ratio of the volume of air to the total volume of voids.

q: 11. The change of moisture content of soils, changes the
options: value of the angle of repose
explain: Moisture content influences frictional/angle-of-repose behaviour, compaction effort needed, and cohesive strength — hence all listed properties are affected.

q: 12. The ratio of weight of water to the weight of solids in a given mass of soil, is known as
explain: Water content (w) is the ratio of the weight of water to the dry weight of solids, usually expressed as a percentage.

q: 13. If a soil undergoes a change in shape and volume by application of external loads over it, but recovers its shape and volume immediately after removal of the load, the property of the soil to be
explain: Immediate and complete recovery of shape/volume after unloading is the defining characteristic of elastic behaviour.

q: 14. The degree of saturation in soils can be defined as the ratio of
options: water by weight to the dry soil weight
volume of water to the gross volume of soil
volume of water to volume of voids in soil
explain: Degree of saturation (S) specifically measures how much of the void space is occupied by water.

q: 15. The relationship between void ratio (e) and porosity ratio (n) is
explain: The standard relationship between these two parameters is e = n / (1-n) or n = e / (1+e).

q: 16. The fundamental relation between percentage Air voids na, specific gravity (G), water content (w) and dry density (gamma_d) is
explain: The formula relates dry density to air voids and specific gravity; the options in the image are slightly different, but 'a' is the intended answer key choice.

q: 17. The specific gravity of sandy soils is
explain: The specific gravity of most inorganic soils like sand typically falls around 2.65.

q: 18. The percentage of the porosity of clay is in the range of
explain: The answer key indicates 'b' (20-30%) for the specific range of clay porosity in this context.

q: 19. The soil sample contains volume of void 0.2 and volume of soil is 0.30 then find the void ratio & porosity of soil
explain: Void ratio e = Vv/Vs = 0.2/0.3 = 0.67. Porosity n = Vv/Vt = 0.2/(0.2+0.3) = 0.40.

q: 20. The water content in a soil sample when it continues to loose weight without loosing the volume, is called
explain: Shrinkage limit is the water content below which further loss of moisture does not cause any further reduction in volume — i.e., weight reduces but volume stays constant.

q: 21. The shearing strength of the following soil will be excellent when compacted and saturated .............
explain: Well-graded sand (SW) compacts to high density with good interlocking, retaining good shear strength even when saturated.

q: 22. The density of soil can be increased
options: by reducing the space occupied by air
by elastic compression of soil grains
explain: Densification (compaction) can occur through expulsion of air, compression of grains, and expulsion of water — all mechanisms contribute to increasing density.

q: 23. In Geotechnical Engineering, soil is considered as a phase material.
explain: Soil is treated as a 3-phase material consisting of solids, water, and air.

q: 24. Compaction of soil .............
explain: Compaction simultaneously increases dry density and decreases porosity as air voids are expelled.

q: 25. The ratio of dry density ............. in the field to the proctor's maximum dry density is called
explain: Relative compaction is defined as the ratio of field dry density to the laboratory (Proctor) maximum dry density, usually expressed as a percentage.

q: 26. The soil involved in the compaction is .............
explain: Compaction is a mechanical process applied to partly saturated (moist, unsaturated) soil to expel air from voids.

q: 27. The admixture used in soil stabilization is .............
explain: Cement, lime, and bitumen are all commonly used admixtures for soil stabilization, depending on soil type and application.

q: 28. The bearing capacity of a soil does not depend on .............
explain: Bearing capacity is a soil/footing property (depends on footing size, shape, depth, and soil shear parameters), not on the load applied to it.

q: 29. A fully saturated soil is called
options: two phase system with soil and air
two phase system with soil and water
explain: When all voids are filled with water and none with air, the soil has only two phases: solids and water.

q: 30. The type of shear failure that can be expected for a cohesionless soil whose angle of internal friction is less than 29° is .............
explain: A relatively high friction angle threshold (~29°) is associated with denser sand behaviour leading to general shear failure per the reference classification used here.

q: 31. The ratio of volume of air voids to the total volume of the given soil mass is known as
explain: Percentage of air voids = Volume of air voids / Total volume of soil mass, distinguishing it from air content which is relative to total void volume only.

q: 32. The deformations of soils under a strip footing are .............
explain: A strip (continuous) footing is long in one direction, so stress and deformation are essentially two-dimensional (plane strain).

q: 33. The deformations of soils under a circular or square footing are .............
explain: Circular or square footings load the soil symmetrically in all directions, producing three-dimensional stress and deformation patterns.

q: 34. If a soil suffers a change in volume by the application of external loads but recovers its volume immediately after the load gets removed, such a soil is termed as .............
explain: Immediate and complete volume recovery upon unloading is the defining characteristic of elastic behaviour.

q: 35. For a cohesion less soil, the modulus of elasticity .............
explain: In cohesionless soils, stiffness depends on confining pressure, which increases with depth, so modulus of elasticity varies roughly linearly with depth.

q: 36. The property of a soil which enables to regain its strength lost on remoulding in a short time, without change of moisture content, is called .............
explain: Thixotropy is the time-dependent regain of strength after remoulding, occurring without any change in water content.

q: 37. The maximum over consolidation ratio of normally consolidated soil is .............
explain: By definition, a normally consolidated soil has OCR = 1, the maximum value consistent with 'normally consolidated'.

q: 38. In a triaxial compression test on a soil specimen, the intermediate principal stress is equal to
options: Difference between major and minor principal stresses
explain: In the standard axisymmetric triaxial test, the confining (cell) pressure acts equally in both horizontal directions, so the intermediate principal stress equals the minor principal stress (σ2 = σ3).

q: 39. The compressibility of the following soil will be excellent when compacted and saturated .............
explain: Clayey gravel (GC) exhibits the highest compressibility among these coarse-grained classifications due to its clay fraction.

q: 40. Standard Proctor test is used for determining
explain: The Standard Proctor compaction test establishes the relationship between dry density and moisture content, identifying the optimum moisture content for maximum compaction.

q: 41. The most effective method for compacting sands is by
explain: Cohesionless sandy soils compact best under vibratory action (vibrating rollers/plates), which rearranges the granular particles into a denser packing.

q: 42. If the volume of voids is equal to the volume of solids in a soil mass, then the values of porosity and voids ratio respectively are
explain: If Vv = Vs, then void ratio e = Vv/Vs = 1.0, and porosity n = Vv/(Vv+Vs) = 1/2 = 0.5, giving porosity=0.5 and void ratio=1.0.

q: 43. Which of the following methods is most accurate for the determination of the water content of soil'
explain: The oven drying method (at 105-110°C to constant weight) remains the standard reference/most accurate laboratory method for water content determination.

q: 44. The relative density of the soil is given by .............
explain: Relative density Dr = (emax - e)/(emax - emin), comparing the natural void ratio to the loosest and densest states.

q: 45. The process of compaction of soil may involve
explain: Field/lab compaction can be achieved through rolling, tamping (ramming), or vibration — the method chosen depends on soil type, but all are recognized compaction techniques.

q: 46. Bitumen, when added to soil, mainly .............
explain: Bitumen primarily coats soil particles and acts as a waterproofing agent, reducing moisture infiltration.

q: 47. The safe bearing capacity of a soil can be defined as .............
options: maximum pressure which the soil can carry safely without shear failure
ultimate load on the bearing area
pressure at which the settlement will not exceed the allowable settlement
explain: Safe bearing capacity is the maximum pressure the soil can safely sustain without risk of shear failure, incorporating a factor of safety.

q: 48. The failure envelope for a clayey soil will be horizontal in the case of .............
explain: In the unconsolidated undrained (UU) test on saturated clay, the failure envelope is horizontal (phi=0 condition).

q: 49. Water content of a soil can .............
options: take a value only from 0% to 100%
explain: Because water content is defined relative to weight of solids (not total weight), highly organic or soft clays can have water content exceeding 100%.

q: 50. A moist sample of soil weighs 24 g in a tin lid. The tin lid above weighs 14 g. Oven dry weight of tin and sample is 22 g. What is the water content of the soil?
explain: Weight of water = 24-22 = 2 g; weight of dry solids = 22-14 = 8 g; water content = 2/8 = 25%.

q: 51. The ratio of volume of air Va to the volume of voids Vv is called .............
explain: Air content is precisely defined as the ratio of air-void volume to total void volume.

q: 52. Which of the following methods give accurate determination of water content?
explain: Per the reference key, the calcium carbide method is marked as giving accurate results; oven drying is also a standard reference method.

q: 53. The relation between void ratio e, specific gravity G, water content w, and degree of saturation S is given by .............
explain: Per the reference key this relation is given as e = wGS; note the commonly used phase relation is eS = wG.

q: 54. The water content of a saturated soil is 50%. If the specific gravity of the solids is 2.4, what is its void ratio?
explain: For saturated soil, e = wG = 0.5 x 2.4 = 1.2.

q: 55. The water content at which the soil changes from liquid state to plastic state is known as .............
explain: Per the reference key this is marked 'none of the above'; the standard definition of this exact transition water content is the liquid limit.

q: 56. Berms are used to .............
explain: Berms add mass and width at the toe of an embankment, increasing shear resistance and stability against slope failure.

q: 57. The ratio of weight of water to the weight of solids is called .............
explain: Per the reference key this is marked 'porosity'; the standard definition of weight of water to weight of solids is actually water content.

q: 58. Valid range for degree of saturations of a soil in percentage .............
explain: Per the reference key this option is marked; the physically valid range for degree of saturation is actually 0 <= S <= 100%.

q: 59. The maximum water content of a saturated soil at which a reduction in its moisture does not cause a decrease in volume of the soil, is called .............
explain: This is the standard definition of the shrinkage limit, the boundary below which further drying causes no further volume decrease.

q: 60. If the pores of a soil are completely full of air only, the soil is said to be .............
explain: A soil with only air (no water) in its voids is classified as dry soil.

q: 61. The unit weight of a soil at zero air voids depends upon .............
explain: The zero-air-voids unit weight formula combines unit weight of water, water content, and specific gravity of solids together.

q: 62. Compression of soils occurs rapidly if voids are occupied by .............
explain: Air is highly compressible and escapes voids almost instantly under load, so soils with air-filled voids compress much faster than saturated soils.

q: 63. A clay deposit subjected to pressure in the past which is more than the present overburden pressure is known as .............
explain: When past pressure exceeded the present overburden, the clay is classified as over-consolidated (OCR > 1).
